head: pr17402-r53
report:
The prior head 86f52f41 is available. Diffing it against the current head to see what changed this round.

I found one low-severity defect at `ca8db136`. All eight findings from the previous round look closed. I only had 20 minutes, so I reviewed the delta from the prior head (`86f52f41` → `ca8db136`, 12 source files under `packages/coding-agent/src`) rather than the whole 35k-line diff. I re-measured two of the earlier findings with a probe; the other six I checked by reading the code only.

## DEFECT: Promise-returning context members refuse with a synchronous throw instead of a rejected promise

**Mechanism.** `handSessionFacade` in `boundary-data.ts` decides whether a member should refuse by rejecting using one test: `fn instanceof AsyncFunction`. Its own comment says "an async member refuses by rejecting, as every other failure of it does." But many members typed as returning `Promise<…>` are plain arrow functions that just return a promise, so the test misses them. Once their session has gone, these members throw synchronously, before any promise exists.
- In `createCommandContext`, wrapped this round: `waitForIdle`, `newSession`, `branch`, `navigateTree`, `switchSession`, `reload` and `compact`.
- In `createContext`: `compact` and `openPlanReview`.
- In the runnerless context in `agent-session.ts`: `waitForIdle` and `compact`.

As a result, extension code written against the typed API, such as `ctx.newSession().catch(handle)` or `ctx.waitForIdle().then(…)`, gets an exception from the call itself, not a rejection its handler can catch.

**Trigger.** Keep the command context and context from a `session_start` handler on a reused runtime. End session A with `runtime.beginSession()`'s release, then start session B. Call each member and check whether it throws or returns a promise.

**Measured** (`probe.test.ts`, run from `packages/coding-agent`, 2 pass):
```
REFUSAL {
 "waitForIdle": "sync-throw:Extension session retired; its callbacks are no longer callable",
 "newSession":  "sync-throw:…",
 "reload":      "sync-throw:…",
 "compact":     "sync-throw:…",
 "openPlanReview": "sync-throw:…",
 ...
}
```
None of these came back as a rejected promise. Suggested fix: when `fromHostCall`'s admission refuses, check the declared return type or always return `Promise.reject(...)` for members typed as returning a promise. Alternatively, declare those members `async`.

## NOT A DEFECT

**What changed this round:** `boundary-data.ts`, `context-surfaces.ts`, `loader.ts`, `model-api.ts`, `runner.ts`, `types.ts`, `wrapper.ts`, `extension-ui-controller.ts`, `agent-session.ts` and `session-tools.ts`.

**The previous round's findings at this head:**

| Earlier finding | Status | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| astra #1: the composer listener loop | **Closed** | `loader.ts` notifies listeners from a fixed snapshot (`Array.from(...)`). The controller keeps one subscription per runner and `#installComposerShapes` never subscribes again. Code reading only; the real-controller probe was not re-run. |
| astra #2: a transferred tool uses B's owner for its abort listener and returned component | **Closed** | `admitToolDefinition` records the owner (`registeredToolOwner`). The adapter's `execute` builds `AdmittedSignal` from `providerCallGate(owner)` inside `owner.runOwned`. `rendererScope` becomes `ownedRendererScope(runnerScope, owner)`, which stops being live when the owner retires and pins to `owner.forSession()`. Code reading only. |
| astra #3: host getter and resolver errors cross by identity | **Closed** | `fromHostCall` wraps the host call itself, both sync and async. It is applied to `handHostResolver`, the custom-tool `model` getter, and through `handSessionFacade` to `ctx.model`, `ctx.models.*` and the session-manager, registry, artifact, memory, modes and UI facades. Code reading only. |
| claude F1: `abort`/`shutdown`/`compact` and the undefined-argument UI members are ungated | **Closed** | The whole context is wrapped with `handSessionFacade(context, session, CONTEXT_ANSWERS)`, and the UI facade is wrapped as well. The probe confirmed that `compact` and the command members refuse after A ends while B is live. |
| claude F2: timers owned by the runtime | **Closed** | `setTimeout`/`setInterval` now wrap with `session.ownCallback`, and scheduling itself is refused through the facade. |
| claude F3: `getEditorComponent` reads per facade | **Closed** | `editorFactoriesBySession` is keyed on the session owner, and `forSession()` is memoized per lease, so every facade of one session shares it. |
| claude F4: a silently dropped nested dispatch | **Closed, measured** | `POSTRETIRE {"ran":[],"errors":["agent_end:Not run: …","agent_end:Not run: …"]}`: one `onError` report per skipped handler. |
| claude F5: the dispatch hold is runtime-wide | **Closed** | Work is now tracked per lease (`lease.pending`, `#sessionWork` keyed by generation). `AgentSession` passes its own `#extensionSession` to `hasPendingHandlerWork`/`waitForPendingHandlerWork`. |

**Suspicions I ruled out:**
- **Shutdown handlers might now be refused.** `emitSessionShutdownEvent` (`agent-session.ts:6587`) runs before `#releaseExtensionCallbacks` (`:6706`), so `session_shutdown` handlers still see a live context.
- **The onSession spread in `extension-ui-controller.ts:675`.** It does `...runner.createContext()`, which now reads every wrapped getter. It runs inside `runner.runScoped`, which only calls in while the current lease is live, so those reads are admitted.
- **`#extensionSession` is read before the claim.** It is read on the line after `claimExtensionCallbacks()`, so it names the claimed lease. A runtime with no `sessionGeneration` falls back to the runner on both the tracking side and the waiting side, so they agree.
- **Callers of changed signatures.** Every caller of `createExtensionModelQuery` and `handLocalProtocolOptions` in src and tests passes the new owner argument.
- **Untested risk:** the new per-handler "Not run" report fires for any extension emit after the last session has released, and `AgentSession.#doDispose` still drains in-flight event handlers and calls `agent.reset()` after the release. If one of those emits to extensions, users would see spurious extension errors during disposal. I did not reproduce this with a real `AgentSession`, so I am not asserting it.
- **Test environment:** importing `@oh-my-pi/...` by package specifier from the scratch directory fails to resolve. The probe imports the snapshot's source files by absolute path. That is a harness issue, not a product one.
